newsitem.title: GERMANY: Trichet-No EMU divergence between Germany, France.
newsitem.headline: Trichet-No EMU divergence between Germany, France.

text.p: Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Tuesday that he did not see any sign of divergence between France and Germany on how rules for entry to the single euro currency should be read.

Speaking in a panel discussion at the Frankfurt Global 24 conference, Trichet said that France had pledged to do everything it could to meet the Maastricht convergence criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
Asked to comment on whether Germany and France had different views on how strictly the Maastricht Treaty should be interpreted, Trichet said: "I don't see the divergence you talk about."
"My own government has said it is going to do whatever is necessary to be ready for the single currency in 1999," he added.
Trichet also said that he trusted the euro would go ahead on time, starting in January 1999.
He said this would be "for the best for Europe and for job creation in Europe, adding that it was crucial to accompany the euro's introduction with the "structural reforms which are needed."
